module.description:
Example prompt-registry receiver (P1-3).

A tiny FastAPI service that exercises the ``registry_api`` / ``webhook``
promotion target end-to-end:

    POST /api/v1/prompts            — register a promoted prompt (the
                                       WebhookPromotionTarget delivery)
    GET  /api/v1/prompts            — list registered prompts
    GET  /api/v1/prompts/{id}       — fetch one prompt
    POST /api/v1/prompts/{id}/promote — mark a prompt production

Auth: when ``PROMPT_REGISTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`` is set, requests must carry
``Authorization: Bearer <token>`` (matching the skill manifest's
``auth_secret`` wiring). Idempotency is honored via the ``Idempotency-Key``
header: a repeated key returns the original record instead of duplicating.

Run::

    pip install fastapi uvicorn
    PROMPT_REGISTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=secret python main.py   # :8031

Then point the prompt-engineering skill at it (skills/prompt-engineering/
SKILL.yaml ``promotion_target.primary.register_endpoint`` ->
``http://localhost:8031/api/v1/prompts``) and reload skills
(``POST /api/v1/skills/reload``). A confirmed promotion now lands here.

Referenced-doc integrity guard.

Fails when a code comment, test, script, or workflow references a
``docs/<...>.md`` file that does not exist on disk. Code prose pointing at a
design document is a contract: when the target is deleted or renamed the
reference silently rots. Run in CI so a change that deletes or renames a
doc must also fix the sites referencing it.

Exemptions: none by design — if a reference must survive without a file,
rephrase the comment so it does not carry a docs-relative markdown path (the
doc scan only matches literal path-shaped strings).

Domain-coupling guard: fail when TRAID-platform vocabulary creeps back in.

Checks src/ and ui/src (plus the Dockerfile) for tokens that couple the
service to the removed trading platform. The legacy alias layer
(src/core/legacy_alias.py) and the legacy phase-plan tables (kept only to
render historical DB rows) are exempt.

module.description:
Legacy-vocabulary branching guard.

The service is skill-driven: sessions name an installed skill and every
domain decision (paths, phase plans, promotion targets, gate evaluation)
derives from the skill manifest. The legacy ``model_type`` vocabulary
(``direction``/``volatility``/``rl``) is frozen history — readable forever,
branched on only inside the frozen legacy surfaces listed below.

This guard fails when NEW code branches on the legacy vocabulary outside
those surfaces, so the invariant is enforced by CI rather than by
convention. To extend the allowlist, add the file with a reason string —
an extension is a design decision, not a lint fix.

SQLite → Postgres data migration.

Idempotent, re-runnable mover for an existing ``experiments.db`` SQLite file
into a Postgres database that ``PostgresStateStore`` will manage. The target
DB's canonical schema (``_SCHEMA_SQL_PG``) is created by
``PostgresStateStore.initialize()``; this script only moves ROWS.

Design notes:

* **Batched:** each table is read in ``rowid``-ordered batches from SQLite and
  batch-INSERTed into Postgres within a per-table transaction.
* **Resumable:** a ``migration_state`` table on the Postgres target records the
  last-migrated ``rowid`` per table; re-running picks up where it left off.
* **Idempotent:** rows already present are skipped (the resume cursor + UNIQUE
  constraints make a re-run a no-op on already-moved data).
* **Type coercion:** SQLite is loosely typed; Postgres is strict. The
  ``_COERCION_NOTES`` map documents the per-table coercions. NULL vs empty-
  string distinctions are preserved as-is (SQLite NULL → Postgres NULL,
  SQLite '' → Postgres '').

Usage::

    .venv/bin/python scripts/migrate_sqlite_to_postgres.py \
        --sqlite /app/workspace/db/experiments.db \
        --dsn "postgresql://user:pass@postgres:5432/autoresearch"

The target Postgres DB must already exist. The script creates the schema if
missing.

functions._ensure_pg_schema: Initialize the Postgres schema (idempotent) and return a connection.
functions._read_batch: Read up to ``limit`` rows from SQLite starting after ``last_cursor``.
functions.migrate: Run the full migration. Returns per-table row counts.

module.description:
Skill descriptor endpoints — the generic skill API surface (ARC-011 P3-001..008, P3-011).

A new research domain is added by dropping a ``skills/<id>/`` directory and
reloading — **zero orchestrator or UI code changes** (ARC-011 §7.14). This
module exposes the installed skill manifests to the UI and API clients so the
*same* NewResearch form, MetricsChart, IterationsTable, and PromotionModal can
render any skill from descriptor data alone.

Endpoint family (all under ``/api/v1``):

* ``GET /skills``                       — list of installed skill summaries
* ``GET /skills/{id}``                  — full skill descriptor
* ``GET /skills/{id}/param-schema``     — the ``param_schema`` JSON Schema
* ``GET /skills/{id}/form-fields``      — UI form-field definitions
* ``GET /skills/{id}/metric-schema``    — the ``metric_schema`` (chart/table/gates)
* ``GET /skills/{id}/versions``         — declared versions
* ``GET /skills/{id}/changelog``        — the skill's ``CHANGELOG.md`` content
* ``POST /skills/reload``               — auth-gated hot reload (dev)

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Registry-backed, not import-time.** The ``SkillRegistry`` is injected via
  ``init()`` (same DI pattern as ``research``/``results``/``promotion``).
  Defaults to ``default_registry`` when not wired (tests can pass their own).
* **Manifest projection, not re-serialization.** Responses are built by calling
  ``.model_dump()`` on the validated Pydantic manifest models — the schema is the
  single source of truth, so the API and the runtime can never drift.
* **404 with installable-skills hint.** An unknown ``skill_id`` returns a 404
  whose body lists the available skills (P3-013 AC, §10 guarantee).

module.description:
autoresearch CLI — operator entry points (P2 Skill SDK).

``autoresearch new-skill --goal "..."`` wraps the Phase-5 generator machinery
(``SkillGenerator`` + the ``PluginRunner`` dry-bootstrap preview +
``SkillRegistryPromotionTarget`` promotion) into one operator command, so a new
research domain goes from a sentence to an installed, policy-audited skill
package without writing YAML by hand.

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **argparse, zero new deps** — no click/typer in the repo; subcommands share
  one parser with a shared promote flag-group.
* **The CLI is operator-local.** No audit store, no HTTP surface: promotion
  confirmations are interactive (``--yes`` to skip), and critical
  command-policy findings block promotion unless ``--allow-critical``
  (mirrors the API's gate-keeping posture — the operator is the approval).
* **``--dry-run`` reuses the generator's existing seam.** The draft is
  generated into a throwaway ``drafts_root_override`` dir; nothing under
  ``skills/`` is touched.
* **``--dry-bootstrap`` is the T5 overlay preview.** The generated
  ``bootstrap.py`` executes under ``PluginRunner``'s strictest workspace caps
  into a temp preview dir; the rendered file tree is printed, then discarded.
* **Promotion records a git tag when it can.** ``skill/<id>/<version>`` is
  created best-effort (skills tree inside a git repo); failures warn and
  continue — a docker deployment without git must still promote.

functions._preview_bootstrap: Run the draft bootstrap.py under strict caps; print the rendered tree.
functions._tag_promoted_skill: Best-effort annotated git tag ``skill/<id>/<version>`` for the promotion.

Bootstrap runner — execute a skill's ``bootstrap.py`` at session start
(ARC-011 P5-005 / P5-006 / P5-008).

The ``BootstrapRunner`` is the first consumer of ``PluginRunner``
(``plugin_runner.py``). It runs a skill's ``bootstrap.py`` once per session to
render the workspace (scaffold/, knowledge/ corpus, eval smoke-check, system
prompt assembly) and writes a ``session_bootstrap.v1`` artifact recording what
was rendered. This is step 2 of the ARC-011 §5.4 auto-initialization lifecycle.

What moves here in Phase 5 (P5-007): the workspace-prep logic that today lives
in ``session_manager`` (``_archive_stale_workspace``, train.yaml/best_train.yaml
rendering, ``{runs_dir}/{instrument}_{timeframe}/{model_type}`` derivation) and
the 61 ``prepare.py``/``train.yaml`` references in ``orchestrator.py`` migrate
into each skill's ``bootstrap.py``. The orchestrator becomes purely loop +
guards; it reads the rendered workspace from this artifact.

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Thin orchestrator over PluginRunner.** ``BootstrapRunner`` does not spawn
  subprocesses itself — it delegates to ``PluginRunner`` so all skill-supplied
  Python execution funnels through one governed path (X-004 D2).
* **The artifact is the contract.** ``session_bootstrap.v1`` is what the
  orchestrator reads to learn the rendered workspace layout, what P5-008's dry
  mode diffs against, and what P5-024/P5-026 reviewers inspect before promoting
  a draft. Its shape is stable and forward-compat (additive only).
* **Idempotent.** Re-bootstrapping a session whose artifact already matches the
  rendered file hashes is a no-op (P5-009). The caller decides when to invoke.
* **Dry mode (P5-008).** ``run(dry=True)`` executes the bootstrap in a
  throwaway overlay of a fresh workspace, then captures the planned writes
  without committing them to the real session workspace. Required for
  ``draft``/generated skills (X-004 D5); optional for vetted ``stable`` skills.

CommandProcessRegistry.description:
Thread-safe registry of in-flight governed subprocesses, keyed by session.

ARC-011 P0-006: ``GovernedCommandRunner.run`` executes inside a worker
thread (via ``asyncio.to_thread``), so cancelling the awaiting task on a
hard-timeout or operator stop cannot interrupt the poll loop that owns the
``Popen`` handle. The orchestrator's cancel handler therefore calls
``kill_all`` to reap the process tree through the existing psutil
SIGTERM->SIGKILL path (``_terminate_process_group_without_communicate``)
rather than letting the child leak until its own per-command timeout.

Written from worker threads (``register``/``unregister``) and read + killed
from the event-loop thread (``kill_all``); a ``threading.Lock`` serializes
the dict mutation across both.

>>> buf = _HeadTailBuffer(8)
>>> buf.append("abc")
>>> buf.append("defgh")

_SessionOutputLog.description:
Append child output under a shared session logs byte quota.

Quota exhaustion stops disk writes, NOT pipe draining or callbacks. Never
delete existing session files to reclaim space. Directory flock serializes
cooperating writers across worker threads/processes; no global session map
is retained. Other writers outside this helper do not participate.

>>> import tempfile
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as workspace:
...     first = _SessionOutputLog(workspace, quota_bytes=10)
...     second = _SessionOutputLog(workspace, quota_bytes=10)
...     first.write("abcde")
...     second.write("1234567890")
...     assert second.truncated
...     assert sum(p.stat().st_size for p in Path(workspace, "logs").iterdir()) == 10
...     first.close()
...     second.close()

module.description:
Embedding-based domain classifier (ARC-011 P5-016 / P5-018 / P5-019).

Ranks installed skills by similarity to a natural-language ``goal`` so that
``POST /research/start`` can accept a goal instead of a ``skill_id`` (P5-017).
The top match is auto-selected when its score clears ``auto_select_threshold``
(P5-019); otherwise the caller surfaces the candidate list for operator
confirmation.

Strategy decision (per ARC-011 Phase-5 plan): **lexical-first**. TF-IDF over
hashed word + char n-grams, cosine similarity, stdlib + numpy only. Zero new
heavy deps, deterministic, offline, fast. A swappable ``EmbeddingBackend``
Protocol lets an LLM-embeddings backend drop in later without touching callers
(the ``LLMEmbeddingBackend`` stub is documented but not implemented this phase).

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Backend Protocol.** ``EmbeddingBackend.embed(text) -> Sequence[float]``;
  ``LexicalEmbeddingBackend`` is the default. Callers depend on the Protocol,
  not the impl, so a semantic backend can replace the lexical one behind the
  same ``DomainClassifier``.
* **Cache on install/reload.** Skill embeddings are computed once and cached
  (keyed on skill_id + a content hash of the embedded text); invalidation is
  the caller's job (the registry's ``reload_all`` / install path). The cache
  persists as JSON next to the registry root so it survives restarts (P5-016
  AC #3).
* **Cold-start graceful degradation.** Fewer than ``_MIN_SKILLS_FOR_AUTOSELECT``
  installed skills, or a top score below threshold, ⇒ ``confidence="low"`` and
  the caller surfaces "list all, let operator pick" (P5-016 risks).
* **Audit is the caller's job.** ``classify`` returns a ``ClassificationResult``;
  the caller writes the ``skill.classify`` audit row (P5-018). Keeps the
  classifier free of the DB handle.

module.description:
Versioned research and execution contracts.

Authoritative Pydantic v2 value contracts for the universal research control
plane. They define *what* crosses the kernel boundary — run specifications,
execution requests, candidate and observation identity, evaluator-owned
verified results, objective policy, and capability descriptors — as plain
JSON-serializable value types shared by every integration direction.

Contract rules:

* Every top-level contract carries a ``schema_version`` naming its contract
  family (``research_<name>.v1``); an unknown version fails with an explicit
  error instead of degrading silently.
* Kernel contracts never embed harness SDK types. No provider clients,
  message classes, or vendor payloads appear here; harness-specific settings
  travel as scalar ``effective_config`` entries only.
* Credentials never appear as values. Contracts carry :class:`SecretReference`
  records, or the ``secret://<name>`` wire form inside parameter maps, and
  resolution to real values happens outside these contracts.
* Mutable candidate data stays outside resolved contracts: run specifications
  bind candidates by content digest (:class:`CandidateIdentity`), never by an
  inline payload.

Input layers resolve deterministically (see :func:`resolve_run_inputs`):
explicit run inputs, then skill defaults, then harness preferences, then
system defaults — with operator constraints bounding every step. Harness
preferences fill remaining gaps and can never widen authority.

Compatibility with pre-contract session artifacts and start-request shapes is
explicit: :data:`LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY` classifies each legacy surface as
preserved or rejected-incomplete, and the legacy readers raise
:class:`ContractMigrationError` when a rejected feature is actually requested.
Nothing the mapping classifies as preserved is silently dropped.

module.description:
Descriptor-relative, no-follow filesystem primitives.

Sensitive writes in this service land in trees whose *contents* are
candidate-influenced (session workspaces, trial staging, server snapshot
directories). Resolve-then-open checks leave a check/use race: a path
component swapped for a symlink between the check and the open redirects the
write outside the authorized root. These helpers close that race on the
qualified Linux target by pinning every path component with a file
descriptor and refusing to follow links at any level.

Link policy (defined here; enforced for writes, imports, and staging):

* **Writes** never follow links. A symlink leaf is denied independently of
  whether its target exists (a dangling link is denied exactly like a link
  to an existing file); symlink parent components are denied; a leaf with
  multiple hard links is denied as an ambiguous alias for a shared file.
  Replacement is atomic (temp file + ``os.replace`` in the pinned parent),
  so a concurrent rename/link swap cannot redirect the write: a rename
  replaces directory entries and never follows links.
* **Imports and staged inputs** (result collection, trial staging) copy

Normalized reason the model stopped generating (R5-critical).

Provider mapping (spike §3.3 / §5):

* Anthropic ``end_turn`` / OpenAI ``stop`` / Gemini ``STOP`` → ``END_TURN``
* ``tool_use`` / OpenAI ``tool_calls`` / function-calls-present → ``TOOL_USE``
* ``max_tokens`` / OpenAI ``length`` / Gemini ``MAX_TOKENS`` → ``MAX_TOKENS``
* ``stop_sequence`` → ``STOP_SEQUENCE``

carries tool/function calls, even if the native ``finish_reason`` says

continuation (``orchestrator.py`` ``run``).

module.description:
``LLMProvider`` protocol + normalized value types + ``AnthropicProvider``
(ARC-011 P1-001 / P1-002).

This module adopts the X-005 LLM-provider normalization spike §4 *verbatim*
(ARC-011 spike §4; this module's protocol docstrings are the record) as the canonical contract every
provider implementation must satisfy: ``messages_create`` (main agentic path),
``complete`` (one-shot insights/Haiku path), an optional ``stream``,
``estimate_cost`` (→ P1-003), ``capabilities`` (→ P4-009 / router P4-010), and
``classify_error`` (→ loop-owned retry, R4).

P1-002 extracts ``AnthropicProvider`` — the 1:1 SDK adapter — into this module.
The orchestrator (P1-002) consumes ``ProviderResponse`` (normalized
``StopReason``/``ContentBlock``/``Usage``) and holds its conversation as
``list[Message]``. The provider translates at the SDK boundary only, so the
Anthropic wire format is byte-identical to pre-refactor and the X-002 parity
suite is preserved.

Design decisions recorded by the spike and baked in here:

* **Anthropic-shaped normalized types** (spike §4 note). ``ToolUseBlock.input``
  is a ``dict`` (Anthropic shape; OpenAI's JSON-string ``function.arguments``
  is parsed by the provider), ``ToolResultBlock`` is the Anthropic tool-result
  block, and ``ToolDef`` matches the ``AGENT_TOOLS`` shape. This keeps
  ``AnthropicProvider`` a 1:1 wrapper and preserves the parity suite.
* **Loop-owned retry (R4 / D-retry).** The protocol exposes
  ``classify_error``; the loop owns backoff + the budget-aware skip
  (``orchestrator.py`` ``_call_llm_with_retry``). ``ErrorClass.transient`` is
  the signal. Retry does NOT live in the provider — the budget-aware skip
  depends on session wall-clock state (``remaining_budget_s``), which is loop
  policy, not provider state.
* **Phase-contract enforcement is loop-level (R5 / §5).** The provider surfaces
  a normalized ``StopReason``; the loop reads ``StopReason.END_TURN`` to trigger
  phase continuation. The defensive invariant *"tool calls present ⇒
  TOOL_USE, regardless of the native finish_reason"* (Gemini can report
  ``STOP`` with function calls present) is the provider's responsibility —
  enforced in ``AnthropicProvider._from_sdk_response``.
* **Not ``@runtime_checkable``.** ``isinstance`` against a ``Protocol`` only
  checks attribute presence (false confidence on signatures). This is a
  typing-time contract; consumers accept it as a typed parameter.

Three places where the spike §4 draft was incomplete (resolved in P1-001, the
only deviations from a literal copy — see inline comments):

1. The draft references ``ContentBlock`` (in ``ProviderResponse.content``) and
   ``StreamDelta`` (in ``stream()``) without defining them.
2. The draft's ``Message{role, content: list[Block]}`` does not match the live
   orchestrator, which builds messages with ``content: str`` (user prompts) and
   ``content: list[block]`` (assistant / tool-result turns).

The bash tool previously returned the FULL combined stdout+stderr of every

module.description:
``OutputParser`` protocol + concrete parsers (ARC-011 P1-010..012).

This module introduces the ``OutputParser`` protocol — the abstraction every
consumer reaches through to turn experiment output (``prepare.py`` stdout or
agent-emitted ``ITERATION_RESULT:`` markers) into a structured result dict.

Two concrete implementations land alongside the protocol:

* ``DelimitedKVParser`` (P1-011) — extracts the ``---`` delimited key:value
  block parsing that lived in ``experiment_parser.parse_prepare_output``.
* ``JSONMarkerParser`` (P1-012) — extracts the ``ITERATION_RESULT:`` JSON-line
  scanning that lived in ``experiment_parser.parse_iteration_marker``.

The extraction is **behavior-identical**: every parser body is unchanged, and
the X-002 parity suite is preserved. ``experiment_parser.py`` keeps the four
historical module-level functions (``parse_prepare_output``,
``parse_iteration_marker``, ``is_hpo_study_output``, ``parse_hpo_study_output``)
as thin facades over the new classes so the parity engine
(``tests/parity/_engine.py``, which dispatches by string function name and
imports ``from src.core.experiment_parser import ...``) keeps resolving without
a fixture re-capture. Mirrors the P1-007 ``results_store`` back-compat shim.

Design decisions baked in here:

* **Not ``@runtime_checkable``.** ``isinstance`` against a ``Protocol`` only
  checks attribute presence (false confidence on signatures). This is a
  typing-time contract; consumers accept it as a typed parameter. Mirrors the
  ``LLMProvider`` / ``StateStore`` decisions.
* **Two methods, not one.** ``parse_prepare_output`` and
  ``parse_iteration_marker`` have different semantics (delimited KV-block vs

module.description:
Opaque keyset-cursor pagination helpers (ARC-011 P0-015..019).

Provides the cursor contract shared by the list endpoints on
``ResultsStore`` (sessions / iterations / pipelines) and the API layer.

Design: ARC-011 P0-016 (recorded in this module's docstring). The cursor is an opaque
base64url token wrapping a versioned JSON tuple ``(sort_key, tiebreak)``. The
``sort_key`` is a value that sorts the same way lexicographically / numerically
as the column indexed by the keyset (an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp ``started_at``
for sessions/pipelines, or an integer ``iteration`` for iterations). The
``tiebreak`` is a stable, unique value per row — the explicit ``id`` primary
key (the implicit ``rowid`` is not indexable in the target SQLite build, so we
use ``id``; for ``iterations`` ``id`` is the INTEGER PK ≡ rowid, for
sessions/pipelines it is the TEXT PK). The tiebreak makes ordering deterministic
when two rows share a sort key.

Decode is **fail-open**: any malformed, truncated, or wrong-version token
decodes to ``None`` so the caller treats it as page 1 rather than erroring.

functions.build_cursor_page: Build a cursor-paginated envelope ``{items, limit, next_cursor}``.
functions.clamp_limit: Clamp a caller-supplied limit to ``[1, MAX_PAGE_SIZE]``.
functions.compute_next_cursor: Return the opaque cursor for the next page, or ``None`` when exhausted.
functions.encode_cursor: Encode a ``(sort_key, tiebreak)`` tuple into an opaque base64url token.

module.description:
Governed subprocess runner for skill-supplied plugins (ARC-011 X-004 / P5-005).

This module implements the **plugin execution contract** recorded in the X-004
security spike (§6; design recorded in this module's docstring). Every skill-supplied
Python file — ``bootstrap.py``, ``parser.py``, ``preflight.py``,
``resolve_identity.py`` — runs in its own confined subprocess via this runner,
never ``import``-ed into the server process (X-004 D2).

Design contract (X-004 §6, verbatim where load-bearing):

* **Invocation:** ``PluginRunner.run(skill_dir, plugin, kind, input_json, *,
  caps, timeout_s) -> PluginResult``.
* **Subprocess:** ``sys.executable <plugin>``, no shell, ``start_new_session=True``
  (process-group for tree-kill). Mirrors ``GovernedCommandRunner``'s spawn shape.
* **ABI:** JSON on stdin, JSON on stdout, exit 0/non-zero. The plugin module
  exposes a pure function; the runner does the marshalling.
* **Capability block (default-deny):** ``caps.fs_write`` / ``network_egress`` /
  ``env`` / ``timeout_s`` / ``max_rss_mb`` / ``max_cpu_s``. Default per-kind
  caps come from ``skill_loader._DEFAULT_CAPS_BY_KIND`` (X-004 §6).
* **Env (X-004 §4.2 — strict):** ``PATH`` / ``LANG`` / ``HOME`` /
  ``PYTHONUNBUFFERED`` / venv ``PYTHONPATH`` + only manifest-declared ``env``
  keys. **No secrets, no ``AWS_*``, no service tokens.** This is strictly
  narrower than ``command_runner._CHILD_ENV_ALLOWLIST`` (the agent path), by
  design — plugins have no legitimate need for any of those.
* **Failure semantics (fail-closed):** crash / timeout / invalid-JSON /
  non-zero-exit ⇒ ``PluginResult(ok=False)`` + audit; **the exception never
  propagates to the server process** (the single-instance W14 guarantee).
* **Path confinement (D4):** the plugin's CWD is the session workspace;
  ``skills/`` is reachable read-only; writes are confined to the workspace when
  ``caps.fs_write == "workspace"``. Path confinement uses ``relative_to``
  checks against the declared roots.

The ``BootstrapRunner`` (P5-005, ``bootstrap_runner.py``) is the first
consumer; ``parser`` / ``preflight`` / ``resolve_identity`` plugins follow the
same contract.

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Sync subprocess + thread offload.** Like ``GovernedCommandRunner.run``,
  the blocking ``Popen`` poll loop lives on a worker thread; the public
  ``run()`` is ``async`` and wraps the body in ``asyncio.to_thread`` so a hard
  timeout / cancel can reap the tree via ``_terminate_process_group_without_communicate``.
* **No env inheritance.** The plugin child env is built fresh from the X-004
  §4.2 strict allow-list — it does NOT call ``command_runner._build_child_env``
  (that one is the agent path and carries experiment-legitimate creds plugins
  must never see).
* **Resource monitoring.** A psutil watcher thread enforces ``max_rss_mb`` /
  ``max_cpu_s``; on breach the tree is killed and the result is fail-closed.
* **Auditing is the caller's job.** ``PluginRunner`` returns a ``PluginResult``
  with ``error``/``returncode``/``timed_out``; the caller (``BootstrapRunner``
  / orchestrator) writes the ``audit_events`` row. Keeps the runner free of the
  DB handle (X-004 D3 — plugins' execution context gets no server internals).

Multi-worker Postgres implementation of :class:`StateStore`.

Owns the canonical Postgres DDL (``_SCHEMA_SQL_PG``) and the connection
pool. The 48 protocol methods mirror :class:`SQLiteStateStore` 1:1; the
concurrency substrate is what differs — a pool of connections coordinated
by transaction-scoped advisory locks (via :meth:`session_lock`) and atomic
``ON CONFLICT`` upserts, instead of SQLite's single-writer serialization.

See ARC-011 P6-001 (recorded in this module's docstring) for the lock /
fencing / connection-sharing design consumed here.

module.description:
``PostgresStateStore`` — the multi-worker Postgres backend (ARC-011 P6-002).

A 1:1 translation of :class:`SQLiteStateStore` to raw asyncpg, satisfying the
same 48-method :class:`StateStore` protocol. The port is **mechanical** at the
SQL level (``?`` → ``$N``, ``AUTOINCREMENT`` → ``BIGSERIAL``, ``INSERT OR
REPLACE`` → ``ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE``) so the X-002 parity suite and the
dual-backend sweep (P6-002b) verify behavior is byte-identical.

Design input: ARC-011 P6-001 (recorded in this module's docstring). Key points:

* **Raw asyncpg, not SQLAlchemy** (D-driver): mirrors SQLiteStateStore's
  hand-written-SQL shape for parity; ``pg_advisory_xact_lock`` is first-class.
* **Connection sharing via ContextVar** (D-connection-sharing): the 48 protocol
  methods keep their signatures. A :class:`contextvars.ContextVar` carries the
  in-flight transaction's connection; the additive ``session_lock`` method
  acquires a pooled connection, begins a transaction, takes the advisory lock,
  and publishes its connection via the ContextVar. Each method joins the
  in-flight txn if one is held, else grabs its own short-lived connection.
* **No ``self._write_lock``**: Postgres MVCC + atomic ``ON CONFLICT`` make the
  in-process asyncio.Lock unnecessary. ``SQLiteStateStore`` keeps it.
* **Fencing support** (D-fencing, feeds P6-004): the schema adds
  ``research_sessions.lock_epoch``; the four post-command write methods accept
  an optional ``lock_epoch`` precondition so a stale worker's late write is
  discarded (0 rows). When the precondition is omitted the write is
  unconditional — matching SQLite semantics and keeping the parity suite green.

Single-host, N-worker, one shared DB (D-scope-single-host). Same-session
concurrency is serialized by the advisory lock (held via ``session_lock``);
cross-session concurrency relies on MVCC.

module.description:
Authoritative evaluator results: receipts, verification, and honest labels.

Model-visible nonces never establish authority: the W11 echo check only
shows that a payload passed through a context that had seen the nonce.
This module binds result content to the server-created attempt and the
exact candidate/evaluator/dataset identities, and issues a receipt over
that binding so any change to metric, gate, candidate, or attempt identity
invalidates it. The receipt mirrors the kernel ``ResultReceipt`` contract
(``execution_contracts``) field-for-field so it can lift across a trust
boundary later; for local execution the trusted evaluator-to-server channel
is the authority and the receipt provides tamper evidence, replay
protection, and idempotent delivery.

Authority labels recorded on every ingested result (honest, never upgraded
retroactively):

* ``receipt_verified`` — delivered through the trusted evaluator channel
  and bound by an issued receipt.
* ``model_proposed`` — authored in model output; annotations/proposals
  only, regardless of any echoed nonce.
* ``unverified_imported`` — third-party or non-evaluator content.
* ``nonce_only`` — legacy echo-verification provenance with no receipt.

module.description:
Multi-seed mean±std significance (P2 ops defaults).

The legacy keep/discard comparison is a **fixed-epsilon point test**: a single
metric must beat the session best by ``global_stagnation_epsilon``. For a
deterministic eval that is fine; for a noisy (multi-seed) eval one sample says
nothing — the same config re-run lands ±σ around its true mean, and the agent
chases noise.

This module is the pure-statistics core: when a skill declares
``metric_schema.significance``, the orchestrator groups repeated observations
of the same config (each rerun with a different seed is a new sample — the
trial-identity hash keeps them distinct) and asks whether the candidate
config's sample mean separates from the current best config's sample mean by
``min_sigma`` standard errors of the difference (a Welch-style test without
the t-distribution — auditable arithmetic, no scipy dependency).

Design decisions (house style):

* **Population std (÷n), not sample std (÷n−1).** With 2–5 replicates the
  Bessel correction inflates σ heavily; the gate wants a *conservative*
  band, and ÷n is the wider-undercount side that still resolves at n=1
  (σ=0 → deterministic semantics below).
* **σ=0 on both sides means deterministic.** Two configs whose samples are
  each bit-stable compare by raw means (the Track-D1 inert-change
  intuition, formalized); σ=0 on ONE side falls back to the other side's σ.
* **Sparse data is inconclusive, never a verdict.** Fewer than
  ``min_samples`` on either side returns ``inconclusive`` and the caller
  falls back to the legacy epsilon comparison — significance gating must
  never *block* exploration, only sharpen it.

functions.best_config_hash: The config hash behind the session's best recorded iteration, or None.
functions.mean_std: Population mean and standard deviation (÷n; σ=0 for n≤1).
functions.samples_from_rows: Collect primary-metric samples for one config hash from iteration rows.
functions.significance_verdict: Compare two sample groups; one of SIGNIFICANT / REGRESSION / INCONCLUSIVE.

module.description:
Skill generator (ARC-011 P5-021..026).

Drafts a new skill package (manifest + bootstrap + eval) from a natural-language
description by calling the configured ``LLMProvider`` directly (per the Phase-5
plan decision: a dedicated codegen module, NOT a meta-skill run through the
orchestrator loop). Drafts land in ``skills/_drafts/<id>/`` as ``draft`` status
(P5-010 gating keeps them out of production until promoted via P5-024).

Safety posture (X-004 §7 / R10 / P5-026):

* **Drafts are untrusted code by construction.** They get the strictest plugin
  caps, a mandatory ``--dry-bootstrap`` overlay preview during review (T5), and
  a command-policy over-permissiveness audit (P5-026) that flags dangerous
  patterns (``rm -rf``, shell metacharacters in allowed commands, etc.).
* **The generator is feature-flagged** (P5-025: ``Settings.skill_generator_enabled``,
  default off). Operator-initiated, auth-gated; the agent never reaches it (T4 —
  absent from the ``GovernedCommandRunner`` allow-list).
* **No draft is selectable for production until promoted** (P5-026 AC #1). The
  lifecycle machine (P5-010) enforces this independently.

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Plain Python string templates** over Jinja (no Jinja in the repo; house
  style is ``str.format`` + Pydantic). The generator emits the same file set a
  hand-authored skill ships.
* **Validate before write.** The emitted manifest is validated against
  ``research_skill.v1`` (P2-001); ``bootstrap.py`` / ``eval_run.py`` are
  ``ast.parse``-linted. A schema-invalid / unparseable draft is rejected and no
  files are written (P5-026 AC #4).
* **Idempotent draft id.** The caller supplies the ``skill_id``; re-generating
  with the same id overwrites the same draft (safe for retry).
* **The LLM is the only external dependency.** No new packages; the generator
  reuses the existing ``LLMProvider`` protocol.

module.description:
Skill lifecycle state machine (ARC-011 P5-010).

Models the ``draft → reviewed → stable → deprecated`` lifecycle a skill package
moves through, with gating that keeps drafts out of production sessions. The
shape mirrors ``SessionStateMachine`` (ARC-011 P0-002): states + events as
enums, a transition table, per-skill locking, and the "server owns status /
audit only — domain side-effects stay with the caller" house-style separation
(documented in ``state_machine.py`` §13).

Lifecycle semantics (X-004 D1 / ARC-011 §8.7):

* ``draft`` — newly installed or generator-output (P5-023). NOT selectable for
  production sessions; selectable for dev sessions only with operator opt-in.
* ``reviewed`` — an operator has signed off on review; still not production.
* ``stable`` — production-eligible. The default for operator-installed skills.
* ``deprecated`` — retired; not selectable for new sessions.

Transitions are monotone-forward except the operator ``un_retire`` path
(``deprecated → reviewed``). A skill can never move backward past ``draft``
(drafts are deleted, not demoted).

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Async + per-skill lock.** Promotion is a file-move + status update that
  must be atomic per skill; the lock serializes concurrent promotes of the
  same id. Mirrors ``SessionStateMachine``'s per-session ``asyncio.Lock``.
* **No DB handle here.** The machine owns only state transitions + returns a
  ``LifecycleTransitionResult`` describing the side-effects the caller should
  perform (audit, broadcast, file move). Keeps the machine free of the store.
* **Production gating is a predicate, not a transition.** ``selectable_for(production=…)``
  answers "can this state be used in this session scope?" — it does not mutate.

Pure metadata: which optional files/dirs exist, which plugins are declared,
and the resolved capability grant per plugin. Produces *no* side effects —
nothing is executed here. The ``BootstrapRunner`` (P5-005) and the
``PluginRunner`` consume the resolved layout + caps at session start.

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):
* **Path-existence checks only.** Resolution reads the filesystem; it never
  imports or runs the discovered modules. Trust boundary enforced at the
  ``PluginRunner`` subprocess (X-004 D2/D4).
* **Back-compat.** Every optional field defaults to absent; existing skills
  with only ``SKILL.yaml``/``SKILL.md`` produce a valid (minimal) layout.
* **Caps are resolved, not authored.** The manifest's ``plugins.entries``
  may omit ``caps``; resolution back-fills the X-004 per-kind default. A
  manifest that *narrows* a default keeps its narrower grant; one that
  *widens* beyond the kind default is rejected (R10 defense in depth).

module.description:
Skill-manifest loader (ARC-011 P2-002).

Loads a ``research_skill.v1`` ``SKILL.yaml`` (P2-001 schema) and resolves its
``{settings.<name>}`` / ``{skill_params.<name>}`` placeholders (G6). This module
owns the *loader semantics* that the schema deliberately leaves open (P2-001
only *allows* the placeholders; substitution happens here).

The split is deliberate (spike G6):

* ``skill_manifest.py`` (P2-001) — the schema. Allows placeholders as opaque
  strings; rejects structurally wrong manifests with field-specific errors.
* ``skill_loader.py`` (P2-002, this file) — yaml parse + G6 interpolation +
  version-compat gate + per-field defaults. Produces a ready ``ResearchSkillManifest``.

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Interpolation is pre-validation.** ``{settings.*}`` / ``{skill_params.*}``
  tokens are substituted in the raw YAML dict *before* pydantic sees it, so the
  schema validates the *resolved* value (e.g. a URL string, not a placeholder).
  This keeps validation errors field-specific against the post-substitution
  shape an operator would actually see.
* **``settings_obj`` is injectable.** Defaults to the singleton ``settings``
  (``src.config``), so production uses live server settings; tests inject a
  stub. Mirrors ``service_preflight.build_service_preflight_targets``'s
  ``settings_obj=settings`` parameter (P1-021 house style).
* **``skill_params`` interpolation is opt-in.** ``{skill_params.<name>}`` is only
  resolvable when a session supplies ``skill_params`` (P2-017); a manifest that
  references ``{skill_params.*}`` at load time (no session context) raises a
  field-specific error. ``settings.*`` is always resolvable.
* **Version-compat gate.** ``research_skill.v1`` is accepted; unknown versions
  raise ``ManifestVersionError``. N-1 support is forward-compat scaffolding
  (a v1.1 that drops to v1) — not exercised today.

module.description:
``research_skill.v1`` manifest schema (ARC-011 P2-001).

This module is the authoritative Pydantic v2 model for a *skill descriptor* —
the declarative ``SKILL.yaml`` that captures every domain-specific decision the
orchestrator used to hardcode behind ``if config.model_type == ...`` branches
(ARC-011 §5.2, §9). One validated schema serves all skills; the three incumbent
ML skills (``ml-direction`` / ``ml-volatility`` / ``ml-rl``) are authored
against it in Phase 2 (P2-005 / P2-009 / P2-013).

Requirements input: ``docs/adr/skill-manifest-drafts/`` (schema
punch-list, gaps G1–G13) and §4 (section-name canonicalization). The GO verdict
of that spike greenlights this schema; the gap list below maps each resolved
gap to the field that addresses it.

Design decisions (P1-007 house style):

* **Pydantic v2, not TypedDict.** Unlike the Phase-1 value types (``IterationResult``,
  ``Phase`` — TypedDict aliases over existing dict shapes, kept mutable for the
  orchestrator), a manifest is a *configuration document* that must be loaded,
  validated, and rejected with field-specific errors before a session ever
  starts. Pydantic v2 gives coercion, cross-field validators, and human-readable
  ``ValidationError`` messages for free — exactly P2-001 AC #3. Loaded manifests
  are converted to the Phase-1 ``TypedDict`` shapes at the ``ManifestSkillRuntime``
  boundary (P2-007) so callers downstream of the runtime keep using plain dicts.
* **``extra="forbid"``.** Unknown keys are a schema-version or authoring error;
  surface them loudly. Mirrors ``research_manifest.py``.
* **G6 split.** This schema only *allows* ``{settings.<name>}`` /
  ``{skill_params.<name>}`` placeholders in string fields (they must pass
  validation as opaque strings). The substitution semantics belong to the loader
  (P2-002 ``skill_loader.py``); this module does not resolve them.
* **G1 / G2 are the only two sanctioned plugin escapes in v1** (spike §6). The
  schema carries ``phase_advancement.plugin`` and ``trial_identity.resolve.plugin``
  slots; any other behavior that resists declarative expression is an authoring
  bug, not a schema gap.

Gap resolution map (spike §6/§7 → this module):

* **G1** hybrid phase advancement → ``PhaseAdvancement`` + per-phase ``Phase.advancement``.
* **G2** trial-identity synthesis → ``TrialIdentity.resolve`` (plugin slot).
* **G3** actionable-blocker / phase-evidence sets → ``BlockerClassification``.
* **G4** per-scope gate bundles → ``GateBundles``.
* **G5** production composite REST → ``RegistryApiTarget`` fields.
* **G6** ``{settings.*}`` interpolation → allowed as opaque strings here; loader owns resolution.
* **G7** marker dir template + JSONPath → ``OutputParserFallback``.
* **G8** success-value marker → ``DecisionVocabulary.success_values``.
* **G10** multi-file artifact bundle → ``ArtifactStoreTarget.bundle_manifest``.
* **G11** optimize vs satisfice → ``MetricSchema.goal``.
* **G12** non-ML subjects/variants → ``Subjects`` / ``Variants``.
* **G13** category advisory metadata → ``ResearchSkillManifest.category``.

Section names are canonicalized per spike §4: ``metric_schema`` (not
``metrics``), ``phase_plan`` (not ``phases``), ``promotion_target`` (not
``promotion``).

Skill path-template rendering (ARC-012 D4 / P7-005 / P7-007).

One closed placeholder vocabulary and one renderer for every path a skill
manifest can influence — the session workspace
(``workspace.session_path_template``) and the promotion target
(``promotion_target.primary.path_template``). Keeping the renderer in one
module is what makes the "add a skill directory, not a code change" guarantee
auditable: a template either renders here under the rules below or it fails
at skill-load time, never silently at first promotion.

Rules (D4, composed with the G6 loader semantics):

* Closed placeholder set. ``{skill_id}``/``{subject_id}``/``{variant}`` are
  the *identity* placeholders valid in path templates; ``{scope}``/
  ``{iteration}`` exist only in ``sidecar_extensions`` (they have no value at
  path-derivation time). Unknown single-word placeholders are rejected.
  Dotted namespaces — ``{settings.*}`` (resolved by the loader before
  validation) and ``{skill_params.*}`` (resolved at session build) — are G6
  vocabulary, pass through untouched, and are not rendered here.
* No ``..`` traversal, no backslashes. Absolute templates are NOT rejected:
  the G6 loader legitimately produces them by resolving
  ``{settings.host_configs_path}`` before validation — the sanctioned,
  operator-controlled escape hatch. Confinement is enforced where the
  untrusted values enter: rendered request-supplied segments.
* Rendered placeholder values are sanitized path segments: request-supplied
  ``subject_id``/``variant`` must not smuggle separators.

configurable root, caches the loaded ``ResearchSkillManifest`` objects keyed by
``id``, and reloads them on mtime change (hot reload). Manifests are loaded
lazily (the YAML is parsed on first access).

``Settings.skills_dir`` (which points at ``{workspace_root}/.github/skills``,
the workspace-side prompt-primer location). The two are distinct:

* **Lazy + cached.** A manifest is parsed once on first ``get()``; subsequent

module.description:
``SkillRuntime`` protocol — the single contract between skill author and
orchestrator (ARC-011 P1-023).

This module defines the ``SkillRuntime`` protocol: every domain-specific
decision the orchestrator used to make via ``if config.model_type == ...`` is
declared as a method on this protocol. The orchestrator (P1-027) materializes
one ``SkillRuntime`` per session and reaches every domain-specific behavior
through ``skill.<method>()``.

The only implementation is ``ManifestSkillRuntime``, driven entirely by a
validated ``ResearchSkillManifest`` loaded from ``skills/<id>/SKILL.yaml``.
(The transitional per-model runtimes that delegated to the orchestrator's
hardcoded ML code paths were removed together with the trading skills.)

Design decisions baked in here (D1-D3 from the plan):

* **Not ``@runtime_checkable``.** Typing-time contract only — mirrors
  ``LLMProvider`` / ``StateStore`` / ``OutputParser`` / ``PromotionTarget`` /
  ``PreflightCheck``.
* **Value types are ``TypedDict`` aliases over existing dict shapes (D1).**
  ``SessionRecord``, ``IterationRecord``, ``CommandPolicyExtension``, ``Phase``,
  ``AdvancementRule``, ``StructuredHPOPlan``, ``SubjectDescriptor``,
  ``VariantDescriptor`` are typing-only aliases so callers keep treating them as
  plain dicts (byte-identical behavior, zero construction churn). The storage
  layer returns dicts everywhere; a dataclass would force ``.to_dict()`` churn
  across the stack — rejected for a "behavior-identical" phase.
* **``session_nonce`` threading (D2).** ``parse_iteration`` accepts
  ``session_nonce: bytes``; manifest runtimes enforce the echoed-nonce contract
  when the skill declares ``output_parser.require_signed_metrics``.

P1-023 references protocols introduced by the three prerequisite epics:
``OutputParser`` (P1-010), ``PromotionTarget`` (P1-015), ``PreflightCheck``
(P1-019), ``StateStore`` (P1-006). All now exist.

(the only post-terminal change is the idempotent ``stopped -> timed_out``

writes*. This module defines the 13-state diagram, a ``(from, event)`` base

existing direct ``status=`` writers through ``transition()`` is P0-003 / P0-004;
the end-to-end W8 race replay is P0-005. See
ARC-011 P0-002 §3-§7 for the design consumed here (the full diagram and
transition tables are recorded in this module).

module.description:
``StateStore`` protocol + ``SQLiteStateStore`` implementation
(ARC-011 P1-006 / P1-007).

This module introduces the ``StateStore`` protocol — the storage abstraction
every consumer reaches through — and extracts ``SQLiteStateStore``, the 1:1
rename of the former ``ResultsStore`` (canonical home moved here from
``src/core/results_store.py``, which is now a back-compat re-export shim).
``SQLiteStateStore`` is the single concrete implementation today; P6-001/P6-002
will add ``PostgresStateStore`` behind the same protocol.

The extraction is **behavior-identical**: every method body is unchanged, the
schema DDL + ``_MIGRATIONS`` registry stay inside the SQLite impl (P1-007 AC
#4), and the X-002 parity suite is preserved. Mirrors the P1-001/P1-002 LLM
precedent (``llm_provider.py`` co-locates ``LLMProvider`` + ``AnthropicProvider``).

Design decisions baked in here:

* **Not ``@runtime_checkable``.** ``isinstance`` against a ``Protocol`` only
  checks attribute presence (false confidence on signatures). This is a
  typing-time contract; consumers accept it as a typed parameter. Mirrors the
  ``LLMProvider`` decision (``llm_provider.py``).
* **``connection()`` is intentionally absent from the protocol.** It returns
  ``AsyncIterator[aiosqlite.Connection]`` and would leak the SQLite backend
  type through the abstraction. No external consumer calls it (only internal
  store methods do); it remains a private concern of ``SQLiteStateStore``.

P1-007 backlog AC deviations (the AC text predated grounding; recorded here in
the house-style of P1-002's ``D-retry`` CHANGELOG callout):

* **AC #2 ("``WEB_CONCURRENCY > 1`` guard remains here") is factually off.**
  The guard lives at ``src/main.py:_validate_runtime_configuration`` (a
  service-lifecycle concern checked at startup, never inside the store). It
  stays in ``main.py``; the single-instance *constraint* (W14 ceiling) is
  documented on ``SQLiteStateStore`` instead.
* **AC #3 names two methods that don't exist.** ``record_iteration`` → the
  real method is ``add_iteration``; ``list_iterations`` → the real method is
  ``get_iterations``. The protocol uses the real names.

Exception policy (ARC-011 P0-008): the full try/except inventory with rationale
lives in the ARC-011 exception inventory (not retained; the summary below is
the record). Summary —
every ``except`` here is either a narrow read-degrade
``(json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError)`` or, in two cases, a deliberate broad
catch: ``initialize()`` ``except Exception:`` re-raises after closing the
connection (cleanup, not swallowing — and it must stay broad to also surface
the version-skew ``RuntimeError``), and ``ping()`` is narrowed to
``aiosqlite.Error`` (health-probe degrade). There are no migration catch-alls:
``_add_column_if_missing`` uses a ``PRAGMA table_info`` pre-check (LBYL) so

module.description:
Shared file-tool authorization: one context for every file operation.

Every path a tool call exposes — read, write, glob, grep, copy, and any
path-bearing tool argument — resolves through the same authorization
context. The context is derived server-side from run/attempt ownership
(the run's session workspace) plus skill declarations; tool-supplied paths,
candidate files, and workspace instructions never grant additional access.

Authorization model:

* ``readable_roots`` / ``writable_roots`` are explicit roots. A resolved
  path outside every root of the requested kind is rejected — sibling
  sessions, evaluator packages, interpreter environments, control-plane
  storage, and shared evaluation assets are excluded by construction
  because they live outside the owning session's workspace.
* ``protected_paths`` / ``protected_names`` carve server-owned state out of
  the writable roots: private evidence, command logs, trial staging, the
  bootstrap and session manifests, and skill-declared evaluation data are
  never candidate-writable even though they live inside the workspace.
* Relative tool paths resolve against the session workspace; the legacy
  shared-root path style is still accepted when it lands inside the
  authorized roots. Absolute paths are accepted only when they land inside
  an authorized root.

The shared workspace root is carried for command-policy plumbing (the
governed interpreter and legacy ``cd`` normalization live there); it is
never an authorization root for file access.

- pruned → still ``pruned``
- decision=keep WITHOUT consistency block → still ``completed``
- decision=discard WITH unknown/empty status → still ``failed`` (legacy

Stands in at the OpenAI HTTP boundary (chat.completions.create).

Content-driven (not turn-counted) so continuation kicks between turns
don't desync the script:
1. no eval output seen yet → run the eval via the bash tool;
2. eval output present, not yet relayed → relay its exact marker line
   in the SAME response that issues the next eval (the marker-relay
   contract: a marker is only honored in a turn that itself ran a
   training command — this is how real agents behave);
3. relayed, not yet forged → emit a FORGED marker (tampered nonce),
   again alongside a real eval call;
4. otherwise → TERMINATE_REQUEST + end turn.
Tool-free calls (the insights path) get plain JSON text.
